**What type of PR is this?**

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR adds a test to test the following untested endpoints:
+ replaceCoreV1NamespacedReplicationControllerStatus
+ readCoreV1NamespacedReplicationControllerStatus
+ patchCoreV1NamespacedReplicationControllerStatus
+ patchCoreV1NamespacedReplicationControllerScale
+ patchCoreV1NamespacedReplicationController
+ listCoreV1ReplicationControllerForAllNamespaces
+ deleteCoreV1CollectionNamespacedReplicationController

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #88302

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Adds +7 endpoint test coverage (good for conformance)

Yeah, this is not surprising at all, we are patching ready replicas and so fighting with the controller. Not sure why I didn't catch that, before. Doh.

Choices are:

 - patch something the controller isn't messing with regularly (not sure what that would be)
 - properly handle optimistic concurrency by retrying in these cases, AND by not necessarily expecting the value we write to be there later
I'm looking into this with Caleb

review_comments: I implemented it this way because it was written like this in [test/e2e/apps/disruption.go:L65-L72](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/apps/disruption.go#L65-L72)

nit: All existing tests in this rc.go file are using `f.Namespace.Name` in these functions.
So it is nice to use `f.Namespace.Name` directly like the other tests and create another cleanup PR if really necessary to cover the other tests.
This comes into my mind because here is a common part for all tests in this rc.go file but this `ns` is only used in additional test code.
Nit that can be addressed in followup PR: this is a magic number that could use some explanation.  Why was three minutes chosen?

It seemed to fail on shorter times due to other tests, I believe.
There was another test where in last week's meeting [this was discussed](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88778#issuecomment-603470581).

> @BobyMCbobs 180 seconds was chosen was initially at or below 60, it seemed.. I changed it to make it unflakey. Happy to change it.
